name: Semi-extended lateral parapatellar approach for tibial nailing
corridor: Longitudinal cut over or along the lateral patella, lateral parapatellar retinaculum divided leaving a few-millimeter cuff, sleeve passed extra-articularly onto the anterior crest to the same canal-aligned start

positioning.text: Position in semi-extension so the sleeve can sit on the anterior crest and true AP and lateral knee images can be obtained.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the patella, lateral retinaculum, tibial crest, and the same canal-aligned start used for other tibial nails: medial aspect of the lateral spine, 3 mm medial to the crest, just distal to the plateau–metaphyseal angle.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal cut over the patella or along its lateral border, long enough for a lateral parapatellar arthrotomy-style window.

superficial_interval.text: Divide the lateral parapatellar retinaculum, leaving a few-millimeter cuff on the patella for repair. Lengthen the retinacular cut if the patella is stiff so cartilage can be protected. The joint capsule is usually not opened.

deep_interval.text: Pass the nail guide sleeves atraumatically onto the anterior tibial crest. Keep the sleeve in for the whole case to protect patellar and distal-femoral cartilage. Do not damage those articular surfaces while inserting the sleeve.

layers.text: Skin, lateral parapatellar retinaculum with a repair cuff, extra-articular sleeve on the anterior crest, then the canal start.

structures_at_risk.text: Patellar and distal-femoral articular cartilage are at risk if the sleeve is not kept in place. A missing retinacular cuff prevents repair.

danger_zones.text: Inserting or working without a protective sleeve against the articular surfaces is the cartilage danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: If the patella is not mobile, lengthen the retinacular split rather than levering on cartilage.

exposure.text: A semi-extended extra-articular alternative to the suprapatellar quadriceps-tendon sleeve for the same canal start.

limitations.text: The capsule is usually not opened, so this is not an articular reduction window.

indications.text: Used for semi-extended tibial nailing through a lateral parapatellar sleeve.

closure.text: Repair the lateral retinaculum to the patellar cuff and close skin.

complications.text: Complications include chondral injury to the patella or distal femur if the sleeve is omitted, and retinacular repair failure if no cuff is left.

procedure_applications.condition: A tibial shaft is nailed in semi-extension through a lateral parapatellar sleeve rather than a suprapatellar quadriceps split

questions.question: Is the joint capsule usually opened in the lateral parapatellar nail approach?
questions.answer: No; the capsule is usually not opened.

questions.question: How is the retinaculum divided so it can be repaired?
questions.answer: Leave a cuff of a few millimeters on the patella.

questions.question: Why keep the sleeve in for the whole case?
questions.answer: To protect the articular cartilage of the patella and distal femur.
